item.title: Turbulence at the Correlation Scale as the Driver of Magnetic Reconnection: In Situ Observations and Kinetic Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the statistical properties of magnetic reconnection using high-resolution in situ observations from the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) Mission in the terrestrial magnetosheath and kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. For the first time, using in situ observations, we find that the statistics of upstream reconnecting fields in a macroscopic turbulent plasma system are closely linked with the amplitude of turbulence at the correlation scales. These results are further confirmed with fully kinetic plasma turbulence simulations. Consequently, the average magnetic reconnection rates and associated heating rates, determined through the upstream fields, could become orders of magnitude higher than those predicted using the turbulence amplitude at the dissipation scale. We then use a simplified model of the heating of reconnection exhausts to estimate the ratio of this reconnection heating rate to the overall energy cascade rate due to turbulence. Estimates from the PIC simulations and the MMS observations yield a ratio on the order of $1/5$, indicating that direct reconnection heating is playing a substantial role in dissipating the turbulent fluctuations.

item.title: Equilibrium Elongation of Charged Nanoclusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.17513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When internal electrostatic stresses from electron repulsions overcome surface tension, charged nanoclusters elongate. However, the exact shape they reach at equilibrium has been unknown. We present an analytical model for the equilibrium structure of charged ellipsoidal nanoclusters via a free energy analysis. Energy maps are constructed that determine the equilibrium states as a function of cluster size, net charge, surface tension, and local curvature. The model is compared with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters having solvated electrons. Despite the discreteness of the simulated atoms and electrons, both the predictions of the continuum analytical model for elongation and the equilibrium elongated shape show good agreement. The model could therefore predict nanocluster shape evolution in astrophysical and laboratory complex plasmas and atmospheric aerosols.
item.dc:creator: Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III, Paul M. Bellan

item.title: Horizontal component of the ion drag force in a plasma sheath
item.description: arXiv:2611.17601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ion drag force is responsible for the underlying physics behind many important phenomena in complex (dusty) plasma, such as void formation, particle alignment in an ion flow, shadow-like attraction between the particles, dust clouds rotation in the presence of a magnetic field etc. In this paper, we investigate the ion drag force acting on particles levitating near the sheath edge of a capacitively coupled discharge in xenon. In particular, we calculate the radial (horizontal) component of the ion drag force directed parallel to the lower electrode above which the particles levitate. The calculation is based on the actual information about the ion flow, which is directly obtained using Laser Induced Fluorescence. The calculated horizontal component is comparable in magnitude to the vertical one, which pushes the particles toward the electrode surface, and is higher than previously expected. This unexpected finding must be taken into account in future research. The very possibility of the measurements we report opens the door for detailed studies of dusty plasma phenomena governed by ions and their flows.
item.dc:creator: S. Jaiswal, S. A. Khrapak, E. M. Aguirre

item.title: Finite-Larmor-radius vortex interaction from {\delta}f to full-f gyrofluid dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.18093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-size electrostatic gyrofluid vortex pairs in a two-dimensional isothermal model, focusing on finite-Larmor-radius effects and the transition from local perturbative to finite-amplitude full-distribution dynamics. An effective response kernel based on Pad\'e ion gyroaveraging regularizes the short-range Euler interaction on the Larmor-radius scale while preserving its logarithmic far field, yielding a finite- core prediction for the orbital frequency. Local-model scans show that increasing the ion temperature relative to the electron temperature enhances gyrospinning and filamentation and drives a separation-dependent transition from merger to long-lived co-rotation. Long-wavelength simulations reproduce the predicted finite-Larmor- radius-induced dip in orbital angular frequency, corresponding to a pronounced slowdown of the vortex-pair rotation. For the full-distribution regime, we introduce a quasi-neutrality-consistent initialization that reconstructs the ion gyrocenter density from prescribed electron density and electrostatic potential. It recovers the local limit at small amplitude, whereas finite-amplitude simulations reveal additional mean-density polarization vorticity, delayed or arrested merger, and a loss of density- vorticity sign symmetry already in the cold-ion full-f system. An independent sign scan of density and vorticity then shows how this nonlinear NOB asymmetry combines with the local warm-ion FLR symmetry breaking identified in earlier {\delta}f vortex studies; for warm ions, Pad\'e-based arbitrary-wavelength NOB and NOB+LWL polarization additionally produce distinct morphologies and trajectories. These results demonstrate that nonlinear density-dependent polarization and FLR physics form separate but coupled mechanisms that can qualitatively alter elementary vortex interactions in two-dimensional gyrofluid dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Rinner, Franz Ferdinand Locker, Markus Held, Alexander Kendl

item.title: Radiation in relativistic plasmas via particle simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.18332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate radiation in relativistic electron-proton isotropic plasmas using molecular dynamics, with velocity-dependent inertia, retarded interactions, and quantum-corrected pair potentials. Radiation spectra from the Li\'enard-Wiechert fields agree with analytical models. Successive scattering events suppress bremsstrahlung even at weak coupling, while jitter radiation becomes comparable at higher coupling for all resolved frequencies. This first-principles framework will help develop radiation models for suppression and field effects that are inaccessible in typical particle-in-cell methods.
item.dc:creator: Efstratios M. Kritikos, Pontus Svensson, Daniel Plummer, Brian Reville, Bob Bingham, Gianluca Gregori

item.title: Generation of low-frequency flows by shear Alfv\'en waves in magnetohydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.18423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherently forced, weak reduced-magnetohydrodynamic turbulence is studied in a uniform plasma to investigate the long-term nonlinear interactions of shear Alfv\'en waves. The 'pump waves' are chosen to model toroidal Alfv\'en eigenmodes, excited by suprathermal particles in magnetic fusion devices. Modes with zero frequency and no variation along the magnetic field are generated nonlinearly; these produce analogues of zonal flows and currents in a gradient-free system. This indicates that quasistationary flows can be generated by shear Alfv\'en waves in systems simpler than those previously considered, which relied on compressibility, finite-Larmor-radius effects, or complex geometry. The saturated amplitudes of the modes are found analytically and numerically as a function of pump-wave amplitude. This facilitates estimates of the critical amplitude above which toroidal Alfv\'en eigenmodes can generate sufficiently strong zonal flows to suppress microturbulence in the core of magnetic fusion devices. This threshold corresponds to magnetic fluctuations whose amplitude, relative to the background field, is comparable to $\rho_{\star i}$, the ion Larmor radius normalised to the minor radius of the device.
item.dc:creator: James M. Edmiston, Michael Fitzgerald, Juan Ruiz Ruiz, Dmitri A. Uzdensky, Alexander A. Schekochihin

item.title: AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.15002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reference capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) simulations provide spatially resolved plasma fields but are costly to generate across operating conditions. We compare the data efficiency of five surrogate architectures--Coordinate MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, Fourier neural operator (FNO), and Transolver--for predicting RF-cycle-averaged electron density, ion density, electric potential, and electron temperature in 1D planar and 2D axisymmetric GEC CCP benchmarks. We assess the number of reference simulations needed to achieve 1% and 2% mean relative L2 error for parameter-interior and parameter-boundary test cases, and examine architecture-specific mechanisms. FNO achieves the lowest or joint-lowest reference-case requirement in seven of eight comparisons. In 1D, FNO reaches 1% interior error with 50 training cases, compared with 100 for Transolver and 200 for U-Net. In 2D, FNO and U-Net each reach 1% interior error with 100 cases; FNO and Transolver each reach 2% parameter-boundary error with 200 cases, compared with 400 for U-Net. At the stricter 1% 2D parameter-boundary target, Transolver requires 400 cases versus 800 for FNO. Additional analyses investigate FNO spectral modes and padding, U-Net skip connections, Transolver adaptive slicing, and PCA-Net projection versus prediction error. The results support FNO as a data-efficient baseline for the tested CCP settings, while showing that the preferred architecture depends on the accuracy target and operating-parameter region.

item.title: Deformation Kinetics of Charged Nanoclusters via Surface Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.17514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-temperature charged nanoclusters deform, primarily via surface diffusion, when surface electrostatic stresses and surface tension stresses are not balanced. We derive an analytical model for the kinetics of this process, based on the cluster size, net charge, surface tension, local curvature, temperature, and diffusivity. The model predicts the deformation time when either surface tension or electrostatic stress dominates, leading respectively to the collapse or elongation of the cluster. Comparison with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters with solvated electrons shows quantitative agreement with a single fitted parameter. The model can predict the deformation kinetics of charged nanoclusters in atmospheric aerosols and complex plasmas.
item.dc:creator: Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III, Paul M. Bellan

item.title: Sign-switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature of liquid jets by microscopic laser-induced cavitation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Localized forcing of liquid jets can trigger Rayleigh-Plateau breakup at low perturbation amplitudes or explosive fragmentation at high amplitudes, while controlled bending in the intermediate regime has remained unexplored. We show that femtosecond-laser-induced cavitation, seeded at the interface of a 100 micrometre-diameter water jet, produces a selectable curvature in 0.4-1 mm long segments. Cavitation rupturing at the liquid-air interface drives fast outward jetting and induces a slower recoil on the opposite boundary, which evolves on the capillary-inertial timescale and results in curving of the liquid segment. The curvature is governed by three laser parameters. Off-axis laser illumination on the jet shifts the refractive caustics and redistributes energy deposition between the front and rear interfaces. The resulting recoil imbalance determines the curvature sign, with a straight configuration in the balanced case. Laser energy offers additional control over the recoil impulse via plasma defocusing and nonlinear absorption in the liquid jet, where the response is bounded by axisymmetric deformation at low energy and explosive vaporization at high energy. Repetition rate sets the spacing between successive cavitation events and hence the length of the bent segment. Curvature extends across the segment for lengths of 6-10 jet diameters; shorter segments undergo Rayleigh-Plateau breakup, whereas longer ones bend mainly near their retracting ends. Our results offer a platform for optofluidic control of switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature in flowing liquid jets.
item.dc:creator: Sourabh Singh, S. Sree Harsha, Prashant Kumar Singh

item.title: A Multiscale Analysis of an Interplanetary Shock from IMAP, SOLAR-1, and the L1 Constellation to Earth
item.description: arXiv:2611.18314v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. Transient, mesoscale structures forming around these shocks influence their energy conversion efficiency, yet remain poorly observed at interplanetary (IP) shocks: spacecraft sample the shock transition briefly, and single-point measurements cannot disentangle temporal evolution from spatial structure. Here, we examine a fast, CME-driven IP shock of 2026 January 19, observed by IMAP, SOLAR-1, Wind, ACE, DSCOVR, and Aditya-L1 at L1 and by ARTEMIS and MMS near Earth, to determine its spatial and temporal structure. At MHD scales, a pre-existing solar wind flux tube is overtaken by the shock as it crosses the L1 fleet. This inflates the apparent magnetic compression ratio far beyond the ideal strong-shock limit of 4, showing that upstream and downstream intervals can sample different plasma and bias single-spacecraft estimates. At kinetic scales, IMAP and SOLAR-1, separated by only $\sim$7 $R_E$ ($\sim$340 ion inertial lengths), sample the same foreshock yet record localized structures that differ measurably; these are the first candidate signatures of large-scale foreshock transients at an IP shock. Further upstream, shocklets appear hundreds of $R_E$ ahead of the shock, consistent with steepening of ambient solar wind waves. Near Earth, the shock-to-flux-tube arrival lag increases to approximately six minutes, corresponding to a nominal sheath extension of $\sim$50 $R_E$, indicating sheath expansion over $\sim$200 $R_E$ of propagation. Together, these results show that the IP shock, its foreshock, and its sheath evolve across multiple scales from L1 to Earth, underscoring the need for multipoint measurements to resolve the underlying processes.

item.title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research in the domain of Physics-Informed Neural Networks applied to PDE modelling has advanced significantly in recent years, providing a wide ecosystem of novel methods. However, one frequent limitation is the inability of PINNs to scale out on High-Performance Computing architectures to address more ambitious challenges, particularly non-linear physics models with turbulent dynamics in large spatial domains. Typical studies restrain demonstrations to toy models with simple physics equations, few variables, and rarely any complex non-linear dynamics evolved over long timescales. Part of the AI community has even adopted the idea that "PINNs don't scale". This work proves otherwise. We present a mathematically robust formulation of Finite-Element-Method for Neural Networks (FEM-NN) implemented into a comprehensive, modular framework: Fuse-PINN. This formulation provides the basis for a sclable parallelisation of Physics-Informed Neural Networks on GPU-based HPC systems. Furthermore, an Energy Natural Gradient Descent optimiser is implemented to allow high-precision convergence. Fuse-PINN is demonstrated on physics models relevant to Magnetic Confinement Fusion, including non-linear convective models with fine-scale dynamics. Near-perfect scaling is achieved on multi-GPU runs with increasing problem size.
item.dc:creator: Stanislas Pamela, Nicolas Pailliez, Emmanuel Franck, Victor Michel-Dansac, Laurent Navoret, Vignesh Gopakumar

item.title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
item.description: arXiv:2611.18508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.
item.dc:creator: Dinshaw S. Balsara, Deepak Bhoriya

item.title: Revealing the Nonlinear Amplification of Radiation Reaction Effects via Vortex Radiation
item.description: arXiv:2312.05580v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radiation reaction (RR), the back-action of emitted radiation on an accelerated charge, dominates the dynamics of ultrarelativistic electrons in an intense electromagnetic field. We derive an analytical formula for the RR-inclusive harmonic spectrum of vortex $\gamma$-ray emission in monochromatic-wave nonlinear inverse Thomson scattering (NITS), extend it to finite pulses under the slowly varying envelope approximation (SVEA), and take the Landau-Lifshitz (LL) solution as the starting point. We find that once cumulative RR on the oscillation radius over hundreds of cycles becomes non-negligible, the laser intensity nonlinearly amplifies RR through the modified longitudinal drift velocity, reshaping the vortex emission. For monochromatic approximation of long pulse flat-top laser, harmonic band acquire MeV-scale red shifts and spectral compression, producing overlap; higher harmonics show anomalous polarization transitions, so the superposed ellipticity departs from the RR-free case. For a $\sin^2$ envelope, the lower edge red-shifts while the upper cutoff stays fixed, broadening the band, and individual polarization transitions remain analogous to RR-free case. These harmonic-resolved spectral and polarization fingerprints constitute a self-referenced multidimensional diagnostic of RR effects that complements energy-spectrum measurements and, through the RR-inclusive scaling law between the polarization and laser amplitude, provide an independent route to measuring the laser intensity. These results have direct implications for bright high-energy $\gamma$-ray sources and the modeling of extreme astrophysical environments such as neutron-star magnetospheres.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Ju Kang, Yu-Meng Gao, Jia-Qi Wang, Mamutjan Ababekri, Qian Zhao, Jian-Xing Li
